orders.judge: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Vipin Sanghi,Hon'ble Mr. Justice Ramesh Chandra Khulbe
orders.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
THE HON’BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE SRI VIPIN SANGHI 
AND 
THE HON’BLE SRI JUSTICE SANJAYA KUMAR MISHRA 
WRIT PETITION (S/B) NO. 51 OF 2020
01ST NOVEMBER, 2022
BETWEEN: 
Govind Nath …..Petitioner. 
And 
State of Uttarakhand & others ….Respondents. 
Counsel for the Petitioner : Mr. Ashish Joshi, learned 
 counsel. 
Counsel for the Respondents : Mr. B.S. Parihar, learned 
 Standing Counsel. 
The Court made the following: 
JUDGMENT:(per Hon’ble The Chief Justice Sri Vipin Sanghi)
 Miscellaneous applications (IA Nos.13152 of 2021 
and 13153 of 2021) are allowed, and the counter-affidavit 
filed by respondent no.1 and rejoinder-affidavit to the 
counter-affidavit of respondent no.1 are taken on record. 
2. Petitioner, admittedly, is a public servant. The 
reliefs sought in the writ petition are as follows:- 
“I. Issue writ, order or direction in the nature of 
certiorari to quash the order dated 10.01.2020 (Annexure 
No.1) passed by the respondent no.1. 
II. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of 
mandamus directing the respondent to prepare the pension 
paper of the petitioner and pay him pension regularly and 
pay the other retiral dues with 18% interest calculating his 
entire service from 14.12.1979. 
III. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of 
mandamus directing the respondent to pay the amount  2 
forcibly recovered from the petitioner’s salary of the month 
September and October, 2018 without any notice to him. 
IV. Issue any other writ, order or direction which this 
Hon’ble Court may deem fit and proper in the circumstances 
in nature of justice and equity.” 
3. The said reliefs squarely fall for consideration within 
the jurisdiction of the Uttarakhand Public Services Tribunal. 
4. Since the pleadings are complete, we direct the 
Registry to transmit the record of the present writ petition to 
the Tribunal forthwith to be registered as a claim petition. 
5. The writ petition is disposed of accordingly. 
(VIPIN SANGHI, C.J.)
(S.K. MISHRA, J.) 
Dated: 01st November, 2022
NISHANT
